source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "In 2024, homelessness increased by a record 18%."
said: In twenty twenty-four, homelessness in America rose by a record eighteen percent in a single year.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "estimated that 745,652 people were experiencing homelessness in the United States"
said: The next year's federal count still found about seven hundred forty-five thousand people without a home on a single night.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "including 266,320 in unsheltered locations"
said: More than a quarter of a million of them were unsheltered. That means not in a shelter at all, but outside, in tents, or in vehicles.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "record levels of homelessness have been declared in Los Angeles and New York City"
said: Before that, homelessness broke records in both twenty twenty-two and twenty twenty-three. Los Angeles and New York City both declared record levels.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "Many Americans who cannot afford normal housing live in their cars or recreational vehicles (RVs)."
said: And many Americans who cannot afford normal housing are not on a sidewalk. They are in their cars, vans, and old RVs.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "About a million people in the USA live full-time in RVs"
said: About a million people in America live full time in RVs. Some do it by choice, for adventure or retirement. But some simply cannot afford anything else.

source: Wikipedia, Affordable housing in the United States
what: highlight "total housing costs are affordable if they meet or are below 30% of annual income"
said: Here is the rule most experts use. Housing is affordable if it costs thirty percent of your income or less.

source: Wikipedia, Affordable housing in the United States
what: highlight "the 2023 Housing Wage is $28.58 per hour for a modest two-bedroom home and $23.67 per hour for a one-bedroom home"
said: In twenty twenty-three, the national Housing Wage for a modest one-bedroom was about twenty-three dollars and sixty-seven cents an hour. For two bedrooms, it was twenty-eight dollars and fifty-eight cents.

source: Wikipedia, Affordable housing in the United States
what: highlight "Sixty percent of workers earn less than the hourly wage required for a two"
said: And sixty percent of workers earn less than the wage needed for a two-bedroom home.

source: Wikipedia, Affordable housing in the United States
what: highlight "Black and Latina female workers earning median wages that are $3.96 and $5.47 less than the one-bedroom Housing Wage"
said: The gap is even bigger for many women of color. Black and Latina women workers earn median wages several dollars below what a one-bedroom requires.

source: Wikipedia, Affordable housing in the United States
what: highlight "coupled with the end of COVID-19 pandemic -era support programs"
said: Pandemic-era help for renters also ended around this time. Researchers say rising rents plus the end of that help made life much harder for low-income renters.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "In 1970, there were 300,000 more low-cost rental units (6.5 million) than low-income renter households (6.2 million)."
said: In nineteen seventy, America actually had more low-cost rental homes than low-income renters who needed them. About three hundred thousand more.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "a disparity of 3.3 million units"
said: By nineteen eighty-five, that had flipped. One advocacy group counted a gap of three point three million homes. Far more low-income renters than cheap places to rent.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "the main drivers being a shortage of affordable housing and the increased cost of living"
said: Housing experts say the main drivers of homelessness today are a shortage of affordable housing and a rising cost of living.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "only Vermont did not have median gross rents higher than"
said: You can see the pattern on a map. The states with the highest homelessness rates are mostly the states with the highest rents. California, New York, Hawaii, Washington, Massachusetts.

source: Wikipedia, Affordable housing in the United States
what: highlight "Approximately 44 million households, constituting around one-third of all households in the United States, are renters."
said: About forty-four million American households rent their home. That is roughly one in three.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "Those life events could include losing a job, a medical condition, divorce, domestic abuse, and more."
said: Often it takes just one shock to push someone over the edge. Losing a job, a medical problem, a divorce. One bad month, when there is no cushion left.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "Many homeless people in the United States work, both part-time and full-time."
said: Many people picture homelessness as someone without a job. But many homeless Americans do work, part-time and full-time.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "Around 44% of homeless people were employed."
said: One federal count from two thousand nine found that around forty-four percent of homeless people were employed.

source: Wikipedia, Van-dwelling
what: highlight "there is usually little to no space for bathing or doing laundry"
said: Living in a car is also expensive in hidden ways. You pay for gas to keep warm or cool. You pay for a gym membership just to shower. You eat fast food because you have no kitchen.

source: Wikipedia, Van-dwelling
what: highlight "Many municipalities have laws prohibiting overnight parking and/or sleeping in vehicles."
said: In much of America, sleeping in your car is against the law. Many cities ban overnight parking or sleeping in vehicles.

source: Wikipedia, Van-dwelling
what: highlight "In Los Angeles, living in a vehicle is prohibited on most streets."
said: In Los Angeles, living in a vehicle is prohibited on most streets.

source: Wikipedia, Van-dwelling
what: highlight "approximately 25% were reportedly living in a vehicle"
said: That is a big deal, because in twenty nineteen, about a quarter of Los Angeles's sixty thousand homeless people were living in vehicles.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "ruled that anti-camping laws do not constitute a cruel and unusual punishment"
said: In twenty twenty-four, the Supreme Court made it easier for cities to punish people for sleeping outside. In a case called Grants Pass versus Johnson, it ruled that camping bans are not cruel and unusual punishment, even when no shelter beds are available.

source: Wikipedia, City of Grants Pass v. Johnson
what: highlight "could not enforce an anti-camping ordinance whenever its homeless population exceeds the number of available beds"
said: Before that ruling, a lower court had said in two thousand eighteen that a city could not punish people for sleeping outside when there were not enough shelter beds. The Supreme Court decision changed that.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "allowing cities to jail and fine homeless pe"
said: That decision allowed cities to fine and even jail homeless people for sleeping in public.

source: Wikipedia, Van-dwelling
what: highlight "Some vandwellers have parked in Walmart and Cracker Barrel parking lots."
said: So some people find quiet places to stay. Some park overnight in store parking lots, like Walmart and Cracker Barrel.

source: Wikipedia, Van-dwelling
what: highlight "to remain in many areas of their vast administration for up to 14 days at a time"
said: Others drive out to public land in the West, where the government lets campers stay up to fourteen days at a time.

source: Wikipedia, Van-dwelling
what: highlight "initiatives, which offer limited facilities and some security"
said: In several California cities, nonprofit groups run something called safe parking programs.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "homelessness for one to two million people at any one time"
said: And this is not a new kind of American crisis. During the Great Depression, poverty and homelessness hit one to two million people at any one time.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "The new policy shifted toward public works run by the Works Progress Administration ."
said: Back then, the government responded with huge public works programs, putting millions of people to work building roads, bridges and schools.

source: Wikipedia, Homelessness in the United States
what: highlight "the FTP operated over 600 facilities"
said: Before that, a federal program ran more than six hundred facilities that gave food, medical care, housing and some jobs to about a million people.

source: Wikipedia, Affordable housing in the United States
what: highlight "units (often 10-30%)"
said: Some cities require new developments to include a share of affordable units, often between ten and thirty percent.
